dossier.public_summary: TESS sees a 2.06-day, 1.99-hour dip that is flat-bottomed, planet-sized and on the target star with 378 consistent transits and no odd-even difference. The star is a 3465 K spotted dwarf whose 2.06-day rotation happens to equal the orbit period and shows a giant spot phase signal, but the dip shape, centroid and steady depth across sectors still point to a small planet rather than a blended binary. The period match and long duration due to the M-dwarf radius need radius and radial-velocity follow-up to confirm the planet and rule out activity.

reasons.why: Difference imaging puts the dip on the target; all suspects that could fake the depth are >19 sigma away and neighbours are implausible_within_1px 0.
Flat bottom favours planet, planet-sized 1.82 REarth, no odd/even difference (0.3904 sigma) and no strong secondary (snr 5.221, depth 281.2 ppm, below brightening 21.43).

Duration 1.99 h is long (ratio 1.52 for TIC 0.423 Rsun, 1.34 for Gaia 0.481 Rsun) but still central-duration range and fit with b 0.028 suggests long but transit-like; 378 transits with consistent mean depth and low top-3 share show signal not from few events.
